gap: No retrieved work studies temporal version selection when validity metadata is incomplete, unofficial or noisy. Existing hard-filter pipelines assume per-version in-force dates are available and that the query's as-of date can be extracted reliably, and no work measures degradation when either assumption fails.

evidence.quote: Germany does not provide a public, legally authoritative database of historical consolidated statutes in machine-readable form

why_unaddressed: The retrieved hard-filter work assumes clean metadata and a regex-extractable as-of date, and reports no ablation in which either input is corrupted. The soft-score work (TempRALM) does not model validity intervals at all, so it cannot address metadata noise for legal applicability.
research_question: When per-version in-force dates are incomplete or noisy and query as-of dates must be inferred, does a graded interval-membership temporal score retain higher version-selection accuracy than a hard in-force filter, and at what level of metadata noise do they cross over?
potential_experiment: A noise-injection robustness study: progressively corrupt version effective dates (drop, jitter, conflict) and degrade as-of date extraction (paraphrased or implicit dates), then compare a hard in-force filter against a graded interval-membership score on version-selection accuracy and end-answer accuracy, reporting the crossover point where the hard filter collapses.
verification_required: Requires measuring metadata completeness and noise in at least two real regulatory corpora; the present search budget is exhausted, so the prevalence of missing or unofficial effective dates is itself unverified beyond one anecdotal report.
